mechanisms.name: 01 Global tick floor (main.go:5453)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: every iteration. Sleeps to enforce 80ms (~12Hz) minimum tick because continuous locomotion made walk calls non-blocking and any `walk; continue` branch spun at CPU speed (13,807 unstick lines in one pocket). Consumes: nothing but time.
mechanisms.verdict: Symptom patch for the deeper defect that decision rate and action duration are the same clock. Keep the idea of a bounded decision rate; the real fix is separating deciding from acting.

mechanisms.name: 02 Control channel + step mode (main.go:5463-5539)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: logs/control.txt polled every 2s (250ms in step mode). Commands: exit/tp/akara/cube/town/hold/resume/step. Consumes: whole tick on batch; step mode freezes all behaviors.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. Sound operational tooling; keep the concept, it is orthogonal to arbitration.

mechanisms.name: 03 Werewolf re-shift (main.go:5540)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: shiftCheck%6==0 && !inWerewolf() && chickenStreak==0. Casts the shift, falls through. Consumes: a key press mid-tick, no walk.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. Instant-action maintenance; harmless, but note it runs BEFORE the data read and before survival.

mechanisms.name: 04 TOWN TRIP state machine (main.go:5548-5708)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: tpPhase != 0 (set by control cmd, auto-trip, trap escape). Phases: cast TP, enter, errands, return. `continue` for every phase except 4/5, so while tripping NOTHING below runs — including the survival tick at 5757. Consumes: the entire tick for the whole trip duration.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger, ABOVE survival in file order. The 48-min silent hang needed a bolted-on heartbeat. Ordering survival below a multi-minute state machine is an architectural inversion — a mid-trip tick can never drink or chicken.

mechanisms.name: 05 TOWN GUARD + autoprogress-from-town (main.go:5710-5751)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: Area.IsTown() && curGoto==0. Asserts route target if autoprogress (patch for the parked-forever bug), runs naked-corpse hunt if unequipped, else sleeps 400ms and continues. Consumes: tick.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. The guard's dependence on curGoto==0 is what made 'errand left char at campfire => every run parked forever' possible — trigger reads a shared variable someone else forgot to set.

mechanisms.name: 06 SURVIVAL tick (main.go:5757-5889)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: every tick that reaches position 6. StatusDead: blocking respawn probe (up to ~18s of in-place sleeps), writes death_state, sets curGoto=deathArea, continue. StatusChicken: drink-first then flee walk + emergency TP, continue; chicken disabled when no drinkables (softcore death-is-the-healer valve). Consumes: tick, and on death, ~20s of blocking time.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger by stated design ('survival runs above/outside the ledger') — but it is NOT above: town trip, control batch, and every blocking sleep in any block all run before or instead of it. Survival is a reflex implemented as a queue position.

mechanisms.name: 07 Area-crossing re-align (main.go:5893-5936)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: area != alignedArea. Rebuilds grid/navigator/walkables, resets ~14 pieces of per-area behavior state by hand (posHist, exploreDest, wedges, gotoIdx, townRoadIdx...), stamps trap fences. Falls through.
mechanisms.verdict: The hand-maintained reset list is evidence that behavior state lives in ~60 loose closure variables with no lifecycle — every new behavior must remember to add its own reset here or misbehave across areas.

mechanisms.name: 08 TRAP ESCAPE (main.go:5938-5952)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: standing in a trapAreas pocket && tpPhase==0 && tp bound && not the current goal && 60s cooldown. Starts a town trip, continue.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. Reasonable seatbelt; note it preempts by position, not priority.

mechanisms.name: 09 AUTO-PROGRESS route (main.go:5954-6019)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: *autoProgress && *gotoArea==0 && tpPhase==0 && (curGoto==0 || curGoto==progressTarget || curGoto==current area). Advances routeIdx via three gauges: runs-dry timer (150s no enemy — can NEVER fire at 12x), level caps, XP-starvation (<100xp/5min). Asserts curGoto=progressTarget. Falls through.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. The third trigger clause is a patch (commit fd7bafc) for the death-resume deadlock: death recovery wrote curGoto=deathArea, recovery was weapon-gated off, and this trigger then evaluated false for ENTIRE runs — route logic locked out by a stale shared variable.

mechanisms.name: 10 CRITICAL PICKUP critloot (main.go:6021-6105)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: *loot && chickenStreak==0 && NOT(corpseTargetPos within 40) && belt dry && no enemy contact<=5 && ground heal within lootradius && claim('critloot',70,1.2s). Walks/picks, continue. Consumes: tick + walk.
mechanisms.verdict: In ledger. The corpse-proximity clause is a hardcoded pairwise patch for tonight's herb-chase-preempts-corpse-recovery incident — corpse recovery has no priority number, so the conflict could only be resolved by editing critloot's trigger. Also reuses armloot's progress-clock variables (see root defects).

mechanisms.name: 11 ARMING PICKUP armloot (main.go:6107-6195)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: *loot && chickenStreak==0 && weaponless && no contact && wearable-for-empty-slot on ground, shunning items within 25 of corpseTargetPos && claim('armloot',65,1.2s). Walks/picks, continue.
mechanisms.verdict: In ledger. Exists ONLY because the real loot block (prio 30) is structurally unreachable at 12x density — a clone hoisted above combat, with its own re-derived safety guards, each learned by a death (runs 18, 24, 26 in comments).

mechanisms.name: 12 CUBE FIRST stash (main.go:6197-6217)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: cubeKey && tpPhase==0 && !town && 5min cooldown && inventory>=tripItems-6 && no enemy<=20. Blocking identify+cubeStash session; continue if stashed.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. Blocking multi-second panel session inside the tick; survival suspended throughout.

mechanisms.name: 13 AUTO TOWN TRIP (main.go:6219-6240)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: tripItems>0 && tp bound && tpPhase==0 && !town && 15min cooldown && inventory full && no enemy<=20. Sets tpPhase=1, continue.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. The no-enemy<=20 calm gate is starvation-prone at 12x — same class of bug as the runs-dry timer.

mechanisms.name: 14 SUMMON skeleton (main.go:6242-6304)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: summonKey && 2s cadence && mana ok && not disabled && pets < live-read cap && corpse within 20. moveStop + cast + verify pet count (5 fruitless casts => 10min disable). continue on cast.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger (instant action). The closed-loop cast verification is excellent and should survive. moveStop mid-journey silently steals the walk from whoever held the claim.

mechanisms.name: 15 GOLEM refresh (main.go:6306-6319)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: golemKey && golemEvery cadence && mana. moveStop + cast, continue.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. Same walk-stealing note as summon.

mechanisms.name: 16 AUTO-STAT (main.go:6321-6384)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: autoStat && no enemy within dangerRange && 20s cadence && banked points. Blocking panel session (open C, up to 5 verified clicks at ~1s each), continue.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. Multi-second blocking hold of the whole organism; the 5-point session cap is a patch for a 20s+ hostage incident. Calm gate can starve indefinitely at 12x.

mechanisms.name: 17 AUTO-SKILL (main.go:6386-6456)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: autoSkill && calm && 30s cadence && banked points. Blocking tree session with per-entry live verification; continue if spent.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. Same shape as auto-stat; the build-list with live Skills-map verification is good closed-loop design.

mechanisms.name: 18 AUTO-EQUIP (main.go:6458-6545)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: autoEquip && !disabled && tpPhase==0 && calm && 45s cadence. Blocking pick/place/verify with cursor-stuck rollback that disables the feature for the run. continue on attempt.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. Closed-loop verification and fail-safe rollback are keepers; the scheduling is the problem.

mechanisms.name: 19 OPPORTUNITY GATE oppFight (main.go:6547-6579)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: !town, computed every tick: contact within 8 OR (threat<=strength && pack centroid within 25). Produces a boolean threaded by hand into exactly three triggers below (corpse recovery, death-spot seek, goto).
mechanisms.verdict: This is combat preemption expressed OUTSIDE the ledger while combat also claims 60/50 INSIDE it — the same behavior has two different priorities in two different arbitration systems. Fold into a single arbiter as a combat utility bid.

mechanisms.name: 20 CORPSE RECOVERY (main.go:6581-6769)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: corpseTargetPos set && !oppFight && 10min give-up cooldown; 3min time-box. Approach: pack-strength veto, town-road blocking strides, field last-mile 2x~1.8s blocking strides, else navWalk. At <=10: resumable 14-probes-per-tick hover sweep (hand-sliced after a measured whole-tick 5s sweep with no survival at the exact death spot), blind-click fallback. ALWAYS continue.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger with NO priority number — preemptable only by what happens to sit earlier in the file. The resumable sweep is the proof-of-concept for how ALL actions should be built.

mechanisms.name: 21 DEATH-SPOT SEEK (main.go:6771-6802)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: !Corpse.Found && deathHuntPos set && in death area && !oppFight; 2min time-box (after a 15-min run burned seeking dist~150). navWalk + continue.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. Time-boxing every journey is the right law; each box was bought with a burned run because there is no central journey executor providing it.

mechanisms.name: 22 GOTO travel (main.go:6804-7413)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: curGoto!=0 && !oppFight && navi/grid present && area != curGoto. Contains: resume-reset patch (gap in goto ticks != stall), 5s net-progress watchdog, fight-through, pet-jam shove, refusal stamping (with town and pet exemptions), town beeline sessions (up to 6 chained 2.1s blocking strides ~13s, key-edge law), multi-hop BFS, exit seek with 40s watchdog + frontier detour + route-skip, phantom-exit square-frame test, entrance hover-spiral ritual. Owns the tick via continue on nearly every path.
mechanisms.verdict: The single biggest walk-owner in the bot and it is ENTIRELY outside the ledger. ~600 lines of accreted sub-behaviors each with its own watchdog, each a patch for a measured failure. The measured laws inside (key-edge stride, hover-confirmed entrance click, phantom square-frame) must survive; the monolith must not.

mechanisms.name: 23 CONFINEMENT BREAK-OUT (main.go:7415-7447)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: navi==nil && 50-tick posHist spans a thin strip on one axis. Pushes toward walk centroid with perpendicular jitter, continue.
mechanisms.verdict: Legacy-mode only; superseded by the Navigator. Discard in redesign.

mechanisms.name: 24 GLOBAL UNSTICK (main.go:7449-7497)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: <15 net displacement for 6s (with navi). Rotating-compass heading burst, 350ms pacing patch, drops exploreDest into badDests. continue.
mechanisms.verdict: Outside ledger. A path-agnostic reflex that historically FOUGHT the Navigator and the entrance ritual (both needed stand-down exemptions). Movement recovery belongs inside the journey executor, not as a rival behavior.

mechanisms.name: 25 COMBAT ORACLE posture (main.go:7500-7545)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: every tick reaching here. packAssess (weighted threat vs army+pools) => engage/kite/regroup with 1.2s/margin-4 hysteresis; regroup retreats via navWalk + continue without any claim.
mechanisms.verdict: The oracle and hysteresis are keepers — honest situational assessment. But regroup walking without a claim means curIntent can say 'combat' while the legs do 'retreat'.

mechanisms.name: 26 Target selection (main.go:7547-7625)
mechanisms.how: Scored, not nearest-first: -4/dist, shaman +600, elite +150, rabies spread terms, poison-immune -500 (deprioritized not skipped), weaponless pile shun with contact exemption, 12s unreachable blacklist.
mechanisms.verdict: Keep the scoring approach wholesale; it is the most 'intelligent' decision code in the file.

mechanisms.name: 27 LOOT (main.go:7629-7712)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: NESTED inside !haveTarget && *loot && chickenStreak==0 && claim('loot',30,0.9s) && no enemy within 25. Approach/pick/blacklist, continue.
mechanisms.verdict: In ledger, but the claim is unreachable at 12x density: a live target within radius 90 always exists, so haveTarget is always true. Priority 30 never even gets evaluated — starvation is structural, not numerical.

mechanisms.name: 28 OBJECTS + waypoints (main.go:7715-7788)
mechanisms.how: Same nest: claim('objects',25,0.9s) && no enemy within 25. Waypoint activation on sight (hover-confirmed, esc closes panel), chest/barrel interaction with 60s blacklist, continue.
mechanisms.verdict: In ledger, same structural starvation as loot. Hover-confirmed waypoint ritual is a keeper.

mechanisms.name: 29 EXPLORE (main.go:7790-7850)
mechanisms.how: Same nest, NO claim at all: frontier-driven via atlas.FrontierNear, commitment-until-arrival-or-stall (12s progress clock), badDests memory, random-far-cell fallback, continue.
mechanisms.verdict: A walk-owning behavior that never claims — the ledger's 'one journey at a time' invariant is false whenever explore runs. Frontier-driven exploration itself is a keeper.

mechanisms.name: 30 COMBAT execution (main.go:7853-8088)
mechanisms.how: claim('combat', 60 if dist<=8 else 50, 0.9s) — the ONLY behavior that politely waits when refused (sleep 60ms). Then: curse pass (8s cooldown), damage watchdog (8s no-life-drop blacklist; Life frozen on 3.2 so Mode is the death signal), hover-confirmed bite/skill-strike, closed-loop throw (selection verified, quantity floor), summoner patience (army-on-it never blacklists), kite retreat, distance-scaled approach pulses, Mover chase.
mechanisms.verdict: In ledger. Rich, closed-loop, and full of measured laws worth keeping — but at 12x density its trigger is warm ~100% of the time, which is exactly why everything below priority 50 starves forever.

rootDefects.defect: Two parallel arbitration systems with no common currency: the intent ledger (claim() at main.go:5347) covers only 5 of ~30 behaviors; everything else arbitrates by textual position in the file via `continue`. A non-ledger block earlier in the file preempts ANY claim regardless of its number, and a ledger claim cannot preempt any non-ledger block below it.
rootDefects.evidence: Corpse recovery (main.go:6592) has no priority number — tonight a critloot(70) herb chase dragged the character off the corpse approach at dist 13, and the only possible fix was a hardcoded pairwise guard inside critloot's trigger: `!(corpseTargetPos.X != 0 && chebyshev(me, corpseTargetPos) <= 40)` at main.go:6028. Combat preemption of travel/recovery is likewise expressed as a bespoke oppFight boolean (main.go:6552) hand-threaded into exactly 3 triggers, while combat separately claims 60/50 in the ledger at main.go:7861 — the same behavior has two different priorities in two different systems.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: With N behaviors and two arbitration regimes, every cross-behavior conflict is invisible until it happens in production and can only be fixed by a pairwise guard edit — O(N^2) patches, each bought with a lost run. No global ordering exists that a new behavior can simply join; adding behavior #31 requires re-auditing all 30 existing triggers.

rootDefects.defect: Structural (not numerical) starvation: the loot/objects/explore blocks are nested inside `if !haveTarget` (main.go:7626), so their claims are unreachable whenever any live monster is within radius 90 — which at 12x density is always. Priority 30 was never outbid; the code path never reached the bid.
rootDefects.evidence: 'Loot starves under 12x combat' (commit 70dbf0e) — the loot block never ran for hours. The chosen fix was cloning loot into two new blocks hoisted above combat (critloot main.go:6021, armloot main.go:6107), tripling the approach/blacklist machinery. The clones even share state by accident: critloot (main.go:6065-6071) and armloot (main.go:6155-6161) use the SAME armlootID/armlootBest/armlootAt progress-clock variables, so a weaponless dry-belt character alternating between a herb and a cap resets each clock before its 10s timeout can ever fire — a live latent bug created directly by the copy-paste fix.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: Priority expressed as control-flow nesting cannot be re-weighed at runtime: a starving behavior cannot raise its bid because it is not in the auction. Every future starvation discovery forces another hoisted clone with re-derived safety guards (each clone's guards here were learned by deaths — runs 18, 24, 26), and clones drift and cross-contaminate.

rootDefects.defect: Preemption exists but resumption does not: when a behavior loses the tick, its progress clocks and watchdogs keep aging on the wall clock, so on resume it misdiagnoses the preemption gap as its own stall and takes destructive recovery action.
rootDefects.evidence: Three independent hand-written RESUME RESET patches for the identical bug: goto's stall watchdog stamped refusals on innocent ground after a 10s fight ('hatch cleared 32 cells he then walked straight through', main.go:6813-6820), exitSeekBestAt aging (main.go:6819), and explore dropping good destinations into badDests after combat preemption (main.go:7795-7799). The death-state resume variant locked route logic out for entire runs until the 'Route may reclaim a completed journey' clause (main.go:5963-5968, commit fd7bafc).
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: The loop has no concept of a behavior being SUSPENDED versus FAILING. Watchdog time and executing time are the same clock because behaviors own their own watchdogs instead of a scheduler that knows who actually ran. Every future walk-owning behavior will re-discover this bug; the pattern has already been re-patched three times in one file.

rootDefects.defect: Survival is a queue position, not a reflex: the survival tick sits at position ~6 (main.go:5757), AFTER the town-trip state machine's `continue` (main.go:5706), and every blocking sleep anywhere in the loop suspends it entirely.
rootDefects.evidence: Measured incidents in the file's own comments: the corpse hover sweep was one whole ~5s tick 'with no survival checks at the exact spot we just died' (main.go:6702-6705) and had to be hand-converted to 14-probe slices; the town beeline session blocks up to ~13s (6 chained 2.1s strides, main.go:6945-6985); the death respawn probe blocks up to ~18s (main.go:5782-5799); auto-stat held the character hostage 20s+ before the 5-point cap (main.go:6355-6357); the 48-minute silent town-trip hang (main.go:5551) ticked the whole time without one survival check.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: Drinking a potion at 20% HP must be an interrupt that fires during any action, but the single-threaded block list makes survival's latency equal to the longest blocking action anyone ever writes. Each blocking incident was patched individually (slicing, capping, heartbeats) — the class of bug is unfixable while decision and action share one thread and one ordering.

rootDefects.defect: Shared mutable variables are the coordination bus: behaviors communicate by writing curGoto, corpseTargetPos, tpPhase, chickenStreak, targetID, and ~60 other loop-scoped closure variables that other behaviors' TRIGGERS read, with no ownership, no priority, and no notification.
rootDefects.evidence: curGoto has at least six writers: death recovery (main.go:5824), autoprogress (5729, 6017), naked corpse hunt (5740), towntrip release (5701), trap-escape/corpse give-up/clear paths (6602, 6689, 6765, 6789), goto route-skip (7144-7148). The death-resume deadlock (route logic evaluated `curGoto==0 || curGoto==progressTarget` false for entire runs because recovery's write was never cleared) and the parked-in-town-forever bug (main.go:5717-5721) are both stale-write deadlocks on this one variable. The area-crossing block must hand-reset ~14 other behaviors' state variables (main.go:5903-5911) to keep them coherent.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: Trigger evaluation is order-dependent and non-local: whether a block fires cannot be known without simulating every block above it and every historical write to its inputs. A goal system where journeys are first-class objects with one owner would make both deadlock classes unrepresentable.

rootDefects.defect: Fixed priorities with no aging or utility: claim numbers are compile-time constants and calm-gates are binary, so any environment that keeps a higher trigger permanently warm starves everything below it without bound — and 12x density keeps combat permanently warm by design.
rootDefects.evidence: The runs-dry route gauge (150s no enemy, main.go:5979) 'never fires at 12x density' per the file's own comment, requiring the bolted-on XP-starvation gauge (main.go:5995-6012). Loot(30)/objects(25) additionally require zero enemies within 25 (main.go:7636, 7721). Auto-stat/skill/equip require no enemy within dangerRange (main.go:6325, 6389, 6464) — banked points and unworn gear accumulate indefinitely in dense areas. The ledger holds are wall-clock (0.9-1.2s), unrelated to journey completion, so long journeys must re-win the auction every tick against fresh challengers.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: Starvation-freedom requires either aging (deferred needs gain urgency) or utility arbitration (value of the herb rises as the belt stays dry) — both need a single arbiter comparing commensurable scores. Constant priorities plus binary gates mathematically guarantee unbounded starvation in any environment where a high-priority trigger's condition is an invariant, which 12x density makes true for combat.

keep: The claim() core semantics as the seed of a real arbiter: exclusive walk ownership, strictly-greater-only preemption (ties can't flap), and every transition logged (main.go:5347) — but extended to ALL actuator-owning behaviors and to journey-completion-based release instead of wall-clock holds

The progress-clock law: every walk-at-target journey gets a closest-approach-improvement timeout with blacklist-on-stall (the armloot lesson) — implemented ONCE in a shared journey executor, not copy-pasted per block

The resumable-slice pattern proven by the corpse hover sweep (main.go:6702-6738): actions carry their own cursor and yield the tick every ~14 probes so survival/control run between slices — this is the template for ALL long actions

Closed-loop verification of every actuation: summon cast verified by pet count with 5-fail disable (main.go:6258), stat click verified by StatPoints delta (main.go:6371), equip verified by equipped-list with cursor-stuck rollback (main.go:6524-6536), throw verified by RightSkill readback (main.go:8038), hover-confirmed strikes via HoverData.UnitID
packAssess + posture oracle (engage/kite/regroup) with margin/dwell hysteresis (main.go:5380, 7500-7533) as the honest situational-assessment input to arbitration
Scored target selection over nearest-first: shaman/elite bonuses, spread-aware rabies terms, deprioritize-don't-skip immunes, contact exemption on the pile shun (main.go:7555-7620)
Time-boxing every recovery journey (corpse 3min, death-seek 2min, trip phases) and the give-up-with-cooldown-and-retry-with-army pattern (main.go:6592-6604)

The measured locomotion laws: key-edge-per-stride, chained beeline sessions, walkCarrot off-window handling, measured town-road waypoints, panel raw-pixel clicks, deaf panel right-clicks, phantom-exit square-frame test for transposed grids
Refusal atlas with town and pet-jam exemptions (main.go:6882-6900) — persistent learned geometry with honest provenance rules
Per-unit blacklists with TTL everywhere (loot, objects, monsters) as anti-re-hump hysteresis
Quest-aware and XP-ledger route gauges (main.go:5969-6012) — game-fact-based 'done' signals over timers wherever a readable fact exists
The damage watchdog by cause-agnostic life/Mode observation rather than immunity lookup tables (main.go:5366-5373, 7896-7916)
GameGone-vs-death discrimination in survivalTick (main.go:4371) and the deaths-without-recovery circuit breaker (main.go:5772-5775)
discard: Block order as implicit priority — the ~30-block if/continue ladder where textual position is the real arbiter and every reordering is a behavior change
The dual arbitration regime: ledger claims for 5 behaviors, file position for the other 25; replace with one arbiter through which EVERY actuator-owning behavior bids
The oppFight boolean and all hand-threaded preemption flags — combat preemption becomes a bid like any other

The critloot/armloot clones of the loot block (and their accidentally-shared armlootID/armlootBest/armlootAt progress state) — one loot behavior whose UTILITY rises with belt dryness/weaponlessness replaces all three
Loot/objects/explore nested inside !haveTarget — reachability of a bid must never depend on another behavior's trigger being cold
curGoto (and corpseTargetPos, tpPhase, chickenStreak as trigger inputs) as a multi-writer coordination bus — replace with first-class goal objects with single ownership and explicit handoff
Blocking sleeps inside behavior blocks as action execution (beeline sessions, respawn probe, panel sessions, stride commits) — all actions become resumable state machines driven by the executor
Survival as a queue-position block below the town-trip state machine — survival becomes a reflex layer evaluated every tick before and during any action slice

Wall-clock claim holds (900-1200ms) as journey ownership — ownership lasts until journey completion, failure, or a genuinely higher bid, with explicit suspend/resume so watchdogs freeze while suspended
Per-block private watchdogs aging on wall clock (the three RESUME RESET patches) — the scheduler owns the clocks and only charges time to the behavior that actually ran
The hand-maintained per-area state reset list in the re-align block — per-area state belongs to journey/behavior objects with lifecycles
The global rotating-compass unstick and confinement break-out as independent rival behaviors — movement recovery belongs inside the single journey executor (Navigator/Mover), never competing with it

Fixed constant priorities with binary calm-gates — replace with utility scores that age (banked stat points, unlooted value, dry belt raise urgency over time) so 12x density cannot starve anything forever

The 8000-line single main() with ~60 loose closure variables — the redesign's module boundary IS the arbiter interface: perceive (one read), assess (oracles), bid (behaviors), arbitrate (one auction), act (one resumable executor slice)
